reason: The text depicts Yahweh establishing a covenantal relationship specifically with the nation of Israel collectively. Key evidence includes: (1) Yahweh addresses the entire people (עָם) through Moses for national sanctification; (2) the passage explicitly references 'the elders of Israel' (זִקְנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל), identifying the nation by name; (3) Mount Sinai serves as a sacred national site where Yahweh descends to meet the nation; (4) the covenant involves national religious structures (priests, collective observances) and national boundaries; (5) Yahweh prescribes collective requirements for the entire people. This is the foundational narrative of Israel's covenant with Yahweh at Sinai—the paradigmatic moment establishing Yahweh as the God of Israel as a unified national entity.
